A senator, Tom Cotton of Arkansas, wants it banned. Ask yourself why somebody would hate the history of 1619 so much.

note.label: Psalm 7: David's Prayer for Deliverance in the Last Days

precepts.why:
David is a mighty warrior, so it sounds strange to hear him plead, “save me from all them that persecute me, and deliver me.” Peter gives the answer. He speaks “of the patriarch David, that he is both dead and buried, and his sepulchre is with us unto this day.” Yet “being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn with an oath to him, that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne”, David foretold Christ long before he came.

That proves David was a prophet. He was not only speaking of his own time; he was prophesying for us in these last days, which means David is on the earth today. His prayer is our prayer too: that the Most High will save us from the hand of those who persecute us and want to come against us.

That is why the psalm speaks of an enemy that would “tear my soul like a lion, rending it in pieces, while there is none to deliver.” Rending our souls in pieces is how the other nations try to take advantage of us: the coronavirus was set up to rend our souls in pieces, mass incarceration was set up to rend our souls in pieces, medical apartheid was set up to rend our souls in pieces.

note.label: Psalm 7: David's Prayer for Deliverance in the Last Days

precepts.why:
Psalm 83 shows who David is praying to be delivered from. “For, lo, thine enemies make a tumult: and they that hate thee have lifted up the head. They have taken crafty counsel against thy people, and consulted against thy hidden ones.” God's enemies take crafty counsel against his hidden ones, the Israelites, and their aim is plain: “Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation; that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance.”

That is the persecution of Psalm 7, the lion rending our soul in pieces. The 1619 project laid out what the so-called blacks, Judah, Benjamin and Levi, have endured in this country: mass incarceration, inequality in medicine, being used as lab rats and guinea pigs like Henrietta Lacks and the Tuskegee institute, Black Wall Street bombed, Emmett Till's death. A senator, Tom Cotton of Arkansas, wants it banned. Ask yourself why somebody would hate the history of 1619 so much. It is the crafty counsel to keep the name of Israel out of remembrance.

“For they have consulted together with one consent: they are confederate against thee.” The nations are confederate together in this, and it is against God himself, which is why David calls on the Most High to save and deliver.

precepts.text: The confederate nations named against Israel: Edom (the so-called white man, enemy number one), Ishmael (the Arabs), Moab (the so-called Chinese), and the rest.
precepts.point: The 1619 project laid out what the so-called blacks (Judah, Benjamin, and Levi) have endured in this country: mass incarceration, inequality in medicine, being used as lab rats and guinea pigs like Henrietta Lacks and the Tuskegee institute, Black Wall Street bombed, Emmett Till's death. A senator, Tom Cotton of Arkansas, wants it banned. Ask yourself why somebody would hate the history of 1619 so much.

note.label: Psalm 7: David's Prayer for Deliverance in the Last Days

precepts.why:
Psalm 83 goes on to name the confederacy against Israel: “The tabernacles of Edom, and the Ishmaelites; of Moab, and the Hagarenes; Gebal, and Ammon, and Amalek; the Philistines with the inhabitants of Tyre; Assur also is joined with them: they have holpen the children of Lot.”

Edom is the so-called white man, enemy number one. Ishmael is the Arabs. Moab is the so-called Chinese. The rest of the nations are joined with them. These are the ones who “persecute me” in Psalm 7, the lion that would tear our soul like a lion and rend it in pieces while there is none to deliver.

So David's prayer for deliverance is not vague. It is a prayer against named nations who have consulted together to cut Israel off, and it is our prayer in these last days.

precepts.text: The wages of sin is death; that has always been the case for the Israelites.
precepts.point: The hidden ones are the key. When you learn your true identity you change your life: less pornography, less marijuana, less going to the doctor, less mass incarceration, no eating pork, no celebrating Christmas or the fourth of July. That repentance is where your power lies, and that is why they work to keep you asleep.

note.label: Psalm 7: David's Prayer for Deliverance in the Last Days

precepts.why:
David understands the sign of the times. He says “if there be iniquity in my hands”, if he has “rewarded evil unto him that was at peace with me”, then “Let the enemy persecute my soul, and take it; yea, let him tread down my life upon the earth, and lay mine honour in the dust.” If he is wicked, God's punishment is just.

Paul lays down the rule David is going by: “For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.” That has always been the case for the Israelites. If you are breaking the law, getting arrested is just. If you are selling drugs to your people, it is just a matter of time before a rival riddles your trap with bullets. If we are wicked, the evil happening to us is just.

The gift of God is eternal life through Christ, but it comes to those who turn from the sin that earns death.

note.label: Psalm 7: David's Prayer for Deliverance in the Last Days

precepts.why:
David says if there is iniquity in his hands, let the enemy persecute his soul. Proverbs shows why no one can complain when that judgment comes. “How long, ye simple ones, will ye love simplicity? and the scorners delight in their scorning, and fools hate knowledge? Turn you at my reproof: behold, I will pour out my spirit unto you, I will make known my words unto you.” God has poured out his spirit and made his words known, so no one has an excuse.

Then the sentence on those who refuse: “Because I have called, and ye refused; I have stretched out my hand, and no man regarded; But ye have set at nought all my counsel, and would none of my reproof: I also will laugh at your calamity; I will mock when your fear cometh; When your fear cometh as desolation, and your destruction cometh as a whirlwind; when distress and anguish cometh upon you.”

The hidden ones are the key. When you learn your true identity you change your life: less pornography, less marijuana, less going to the doctor, less mass incarceration, no eating pork, no celebrating Christmas or the fourth of July. That repentance is where your power lies, and that is why they work to keep you asleep. Turn at his reproof now, before the fear comes as desolation.

precepts.text: The heathen rage and the kings take counsel against the Lord's anointed, which is Christ and now the followers of Christ.
precepts.point: He prays for the sake of the Israelites that the Lord will return, bring judgment on our enemies, and compass us round about with his angels.

note.label: Psalm 7: David's Prayer for Deliverance in the Last Days

precepts.why:
David asks the Most High to “Arise, O Lord, in thine anger, lift up thyself because of the rage of mine enemies”. Psalm 2 shows that rage: “Why do the heathen rage, and the people imagine a vain thing? The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together, against the Lord, and against his anointed”.

The heathen rage and the kings take counsel against the Lord's anointed. That anointed is Christ, and now it is the followers of Christ. The same rage David felt from his enemies is the rage of the kings of the earth against the Lord and against his people.

So when David prays for the Lord to “awake for me to the judgment that thou hast commanded”, that judgment is redemption and salvation for his people. He prays for the sake of the Israelites that the Lord will return and bring judgment on our enemies.

precepts.text: The angel of the Lord encamps around those who fear him and delivers them; this is the protection David prays for.
precepts.point: He prays for the sake of the Israelites that the Lord will return, bring judgment on our enemies, and compass us round about with his angels.

note.label: Psalm 7: David's Prayer for Deliverance in the Last Days

precepts.why:
David prays for the Most High to arise and awake to the judgment he has commanded. Part of that prayer is protection: “The angel of the Lord encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them.”

That is the protection David asks for. He prays for the sake of the Israelites that the Lord will return, bring judgment on our enemies, and compass us round about with his angels. Those who fear the Most High are encamped about and delivered, while judgment falls on the enemies raging against them.

precepts.text: My son, have you sinned? Do so no more, and pray pardon for your former sins; flee from sin as from a serpent.
precepts.point: Many of us are still plagued by things from our past even in the truth, whether health issues like cancer or an STD, or the burden of having children with a wicked woman and enduring her wickedness. You bear that cross and follow Christ.

note.label: Psalm 7: David's Prayer for Deliverance in the Last Days

precepts.why:
David prays, “judge me, O Lord, according to my righteousness, and according to mine integrity that is in me.” Ecclesiasticus tells you how to get there: “My son, hast thou sinned? do so no more, but ask pardon for thy former sins. Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent: for if thou comest too near it, it will bite thee: the teeth thereof are as the teeth of a lion, slaying the souls of men.”

This is your prayer: ask the Lord to judge you based on your righteousness and the integrity now in you, and to pardon your former sins. Have you sinned? Do so no more, and flee from sin as from a serpent, because if you come too near it, it will bite you.

Many of us are still plagued by things from our past even in the truth, whether health issues like cancer or an STD, or the burden of having children with a wicked woman and enduring her wickedness. The serpent bit, and the teeth are as the teeth of a lion. You bear that cross and follow Christ, asking pardon for the former sins and doing so no more.

precepts.text: Some people's iniquity will not be purged until they die; do not be the example God has to make.
precepts.point: The only way the wickedness of the wicked comes to an end is that they die. The wicked is the so-called white man according to the bible, and his end is inevitable. This is God's word, not man's; do not try to get God's enemy out of the way.

note.label: Psalm 7: David's Prayer for Deliverance in the Last Days

precepts.why:
David asks, “Oh let the wickedness of the wicked come to an end”. The only way the wickedness of the wicked comes to an end is that they die. Isaiah heard it from the Lord: “And it was revealed in mine ears by the Lord of hosts, Surely this iniquity shall not be purged from you till ye die, saith the Lord God of hosts.”

Some people's iniquity will not be purged until they die. That is why the wicked must come to an end for the wickedness to end. Do not be the example God has to make.

David says “the righteous God trieth the hearts and reins.” God judges the thoughts, so we must change our mindset and move forward in righteousness, so that our iniquity is purged by repentance and not by death.

precepts.text: The house of Jacob is a fire and Esau is stubble; none of the house of Esau shall remain, for the Lord has spoken it.

note.label: Psalm 7: David's Prayer for Deliverance in the Last Days

precepts.why:
The wicked in Psalm 7:9 is the so-called white man according to the bible, and his end is inevitable. Obadiah spells it out: “And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble, and they shall kindle in them, and devour them; and there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau; for the Lord hath spoken it.”

The house of Jacob is a fire and Esau is stubble. None of the house of Esau shall remain. That is how the wickedness of the wicked comes to an end, and how the just are established.

This is God's word, not man's: “for the Lord hath spoken it.” Do not try to get God's enemy out of the way yourself. The Most High has already declared the end of Esau.

precepts.text: Though hand join in hand, the wicked shall not go unpunished, but the seed of the righteous shall be delivered.
precepts.point: The only way the wickedness of the wicked comes to an end is that they die. The wicked is the so-called white man according to the bible, and his end is inevitable. This is God's word, not man's; do not try to get God's enemy out of the way.

note.label: Psalm 7: David's Prayer for Deliverance in the Last Days

precepts.why:
“Though hand join in hand, the wicked shall not be unpunished: but the seed of the righteous shall be delivered.” The wicked may join together, hand in hand, but they will not go unpunished. That is the answer to David's prayer that the wickedness of the wicked come to an end.

And the other half of his prayer, “but establish the just”, is answered too: the seed of the righteous shall be delivered. The righteous God tries the hearts and reins, so he knows who is just and who is wicked, and each gets his end.

precepts.text: The dead are judged out of the books according to their works, set beside the book of life.
precepts.point: The righteous are saved by being judged out of the book of life alongside the record of their works. Christianity is worse than crack cocaine because it tells our people to believe on Christ while keeping no commandments, setting them on the path to destruction.

note.label: Psalm 7: David's Prayer for Deliverance in the Last Days

precepts.why:
“My defence is of God, which saveth the upright in heart.” To be upright in heart is to be righteous, and John shows how the righteous are saved: “And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before God; and the books were opened: and another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works.”

The dead are judged out of the books according to their works, set beside the book of life. Salvation is not by belief alone; the record of your works stands next to the book of life.

That is why Christianity is worse than crack cocaine. It tells our people to believe on Christ while keeping no commandments, setting them on the path to destruction, when the judgment is according to works. God saves the upright in heart, those whose works show it.

precepts.text: The foolish shall not stand in his sight; God hates all workers of iniquity, and iniquity is sin.
precepts.point: The righteous are saved by being judged out of the book of life alongside the record of their works. Christianity is worse than crack cocaine because it tells our people to believe on Christ while keeping no commandments, setting them on the path to destruction.

note.label: Psalm 7: David's Prayer for Deliverance in the Last Days

precepts.why:
God “saveth the upright in heart”, and Psalm 5 shows the other side: “The foolish shall not stand in thy sight: thou hatest all workers of iniquity.” Iniquity is sin. God hates all workers of sin, and the foolish shall not stand in his sight.

So the defence of God is for the upright in heart, the righteous. Those who keep believing on Christ while working iniquity, as Christianity teaches our people, are not the upright in heart; they are the workers of iniquity that God hates, and they will not stand in his sight.

precepts.text: They that are whole need no physician; Christ came not to call the righteous but sinners to repentance.
precepts.point: Christ sat with sinners, but he was correcting them and showing them righteousness, not indulging their sin. We go to the streets to talk with sinners and give them the scriptures the same way.

note.label: Psalm 7: David's Prayer for Deliverance in the Last Days

precepts.why:
“God judgeth the righteous, and God is angry with the wicked every day.” Yet every day you wake up, thank God for his son Jesus the Christ, because that mercy is holding back his fury and giving even those who disrespect Christ a chance to repent.

Christ showed that mercy: “They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick. But go ye and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”

Christ sat with sinners, but he was correcting them and showing them righteousness, not indulging their sin. He called them to repentance. We go to the streets to talk with sinners and give them the scriptures the same way, while God's anger with the wicked is held back by that mercy.

precepts.text: Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, the hearts of men are set to do evil; grace differs for each person.
precepts.point: Christ sat with sinners, but he was correcting them and showing them righteousness, not indulging their sin. We go to the streets to talk with sinners and give them the scriptures the same way.

note.label: Psalm 7: David's Prayer for Deliverance in the Last Days

precepts.why:
God is angry with the wicked every day, but he does not strike every day. “Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.”

Because the sentence does not come right away, the hearts of men are set to do evil. They mistake the mercy for approval. The grace differs for each person; that space to repent is not the same for everyone, so do not take the delay as a sign that God is not angry.

That mercy is Christ. Every day we wake up, thank God for his son, because it is his mercy holding back the fury and giving even those who disrespect Christ a chance to repent before the sentence is executed.

precepts.text: Those who abused God's ways and cast his words away shall dwell in torment; having had liberty and despised repentance, they shall know it after death by pain.
precepts.point: Christ sat with sinners, but he was correcting them and showing them righteousness, not indulging their sin. We go to the streets to talk with sinners and give them the scriptures the same way.

note.label: Psalm 7: David's Prayer for Deliverance in the Last Days

precepts.why:
Ezra shows what happens when the space for repentance is over. “Then shall they be in pitiful case, which now have abused my ways: and they that have cast them away despitefully shall dwell in torments. For such as in their life have received benefits, and have not known me; And they that have loathed my law, while they had yet liberty, and, when as yet place of repentance was open unto them, understood not, but despised it; The same must know it after death by pain.”

Those who abused God's ways and cast his words away shall dwell in torment. They had liberty and a place of repentance open to them, and they despised it; so they must know it after death by pain.

That is the end of the wicked God is angry with every day. The mercy of Christ holds back his fury now and keeps the place of repentance open. Those who use that time to repent are judged as the righteous; those who loathe his law while they have liberty know it after death.
